entries.gave: Read the Cut, docs/product-vision.md to its end, and both kept mores. The people: the accountants, who print a client invoice from their spreadsheet lines at the client tax rate, and the installer, a developer who sets invoicer up on each accountant machine; with the vision, invoicer maintainers weigh a change by the key results.
Read product-vision best-practice.md with its template.md, and refactor-doc best-practice.md, to their end.
The job, from the Cut job decision: invoicer gives the accountant a command that prints a client invoice from the spreadsheet lines at that client tax rate.
Each role named by the part of the job it comes for, accountant and installer, as the Cut roles decision gives them.
The accountant prints only once someone has set invoicer up; the Cut names that someone as the installer role, who installs Python and invoicer on each accountant machine.
No person job is left unclear: the person gave both jobs, so nothing to ask.
No split: every accountant counts a printed, correct invoice as the job done, and every installer a machine where the command runs.
No merge: accountant and installer count different results as their job done.
Two roles, so neither is named user.
Objectives as the Cut gives them: O1 the accountant sends each client a correct invoice without a developer help; O2 the installer gets an accountant machine ready to print without further help.
Asked why: printing matters as each client gets a correct invoice, an end in the accountant work, not something invoicer does.
Two distinct ends, as the installer can finish a setup that no one yet prints with, so two objectives.
Tasks from the Cut: O1 from the spreadsheet lines and rate to the printed invoice; O2 from a bare machine to the command running for the accountant.
How well, as the share that fails: KR1.1 invoices not printed without a developer help or with a wrong total; KR2.1 setups after which the command does not run.
How fast: KR1.2 time from opening the spreadsheet to the printed invoice, own time included; KR2.2 installer time from starting a setup to the command running.
Each key result: Lower is better.
Ranked within each objective, KR1.1 before KR1.2 and KR2.1 before KR2.2, stated once in the ranking line; no order across objectives, as each piece of work serves one objective.
No targets, with the template line giving the plain reason.
Pieces of work from the Cut: the invoice command, the README part for the accountant, and the README setup section.
The command and the README accountant part serve O1; the README setup section serves O2.
O1 and O2 stay apart: the setup section serves O2 without O1, so no merge.
No piece names more than one objective, so nothing to split.
Every piece serves an objective, so nothing to ask.
The person gave the one way and the ideas, held in the Cut decisions 5/0 and 5/1, so no new question.
The one way, as the accountant sees it: invoicer prints the finished invoice from the lines as the spreadsheet holds them, plus the client tax rate.
Three ideas from the person, each with what it gives: the spreadsheet as it is, nothing wrong prints, the rate given each time.
Moments from the Cut: installer installs and sees the command run; accountant gives lines and rate; invoice prints, or a message names what to fix and they run again.
Each moment has an idea: setup by the sheet as it is and the rate each time, giving by the sheet as it is, the result by nothing wrong prints.
No idea proposed beyond the person ideas, so nothing to ask.
All three ideas kept: taking any out leaves a moment where the one way fails.
docs/product-vision.md read to its end. Roles: who the command serves; Objectives and key results: what each role reaches and how a change is weighed; Concept: the one way and its ideas.
Readers from the Cut name: the accounting team, who check the vision says what they get; invoicer maintainers, who weigh a change by it.
Accountants know invoices, spreadsheets and tax rates, not Python or OKRs; maintainers know Python and invoicer, and come to learn which key result a change must not worsen.
The three template sections each hold one topic; no split, as the template fixes them.
The item a maintainer looks for, the order of the key results, sits in the ranking line under Objectives and key results; the template gives it no heading of its own.
Roles, objectives with key results, and ideas are items in no order: bulleted lists. The order reason stays in prose, as it argues by since.
Readers words from the person request and answers: invoice lines, spreadsheet, tax rate, print, install Python and invoicer.
Words kept from the readers; help is a developer help throughout, as O1 says.
Facts stated twice: the key results order, in the KR1.2 and KR2.2 notes and the ranking line; the help O1 rules out, in O1 and KR1.1.
The order goes in the ranking line alone, by the Cut key results decision; the help is a developer help in both O1 and KR1.1.
The two help wordings differ; the Cut decision settles it as without a developer help, so nothing to ask.
Names: invoicer, invoicer command, accountant, installer, accountant machine, spreadsheet, invoice lines, tax rate; each one thing.
Kept the names of the Cut naming decision 0/3; no thing has a second name.
No name refers to two things.

Decided: each Cut decision taken as it stands; the order of the key results goes in the ranking line alone, per objective, with the reason no order runs across objectives; KR1.1 says a developer help as O1 does. No point left open.
With invoicer taken out, O1 reads as sending each client a correct invoice and O2 as getting a machine ready to print; neither reads as a feature.
Each sentence says what the accountant or installer does and gets; none would change if invoicer insides changed.

An E2E run records: KR1.1 each invoice not printed without a developer, or printed with a wrong total; KR1.2 the times the spreadsheet opens and the invoice prints; KR2.1 each setup whose command fails to run; KR2.2 the times a setup starts and the command first runs.
At the moment a line cannot be read, whether to guess it is decided by nothing wrong prints: invoicer prints nothing and names the line; the ideas decide each moment one way.
Headings are the template ones, Roles, Objectives and key results, Concept, each naming the thing a reader looks for.
The template takes no opening line under its headings; each first line, the first role, objective or the one way, already says what the section gives.
Read headings and first lines for each purpose: a maintainer weighing a change finds the order under Objectives and key results; an accountant finds their job under Roles.
Each sentence has a reader: the ranked after notes were no longer needed once the ranking line holds the order, so none marked beyond them.
The ranked after notes state a fact the ranking line states, so no other document is needed for them.
No sentence moves to another document in docs/product-vision.md.
No sentence states a fact found nowhere else that needs a place outside, so nothing to ask.
Cut the ranked after notes on KR1.2 and KR2.2, as the ranking line states their order.
No filler words found within the kept sentences.
Articles and that kept in every sentence.
docs/product-vision.md read to its end as each reader: the maintainer still finds the full order in the ranking line after the notes were cut.
The order sentences follow the key results list they rank, and the cross-objective sentence follows the ranking line it qualifies.
Nothing depends on a source outside the document.
Each sentence opens with what the reader knows, such as Within O1 before KR1.1 comes first.
Conditions come first, such as where invoicer cannot read a line and each time the accountant prints.
The exception to the ranking rule, no order across objectives, comes right after the rule.
docs/product-vision.md read to its end from the top; no place needed a look back or ahead.
Lists kept as bullets, one item for each role, objective, key result and idea; the order stays one prose line, as the template sets.
No sequence to draw, so no sequence diagram.
No structure to draw, so no structure diagram.
The cross-objective order split into two sentences: no order between O1 and O2, then why a change weighs only its own objective key results.
Actors are subjects with active verbs, such as each piece of work serves one objective and a change weighs its key results.
Pronouns checked; that objective refers to the one objective named just before.
No noun made from a verb left where the verb reads better.
Each object sits next to its verb.
docs/product-vision.md read to its end as a machine translator; the ranking line now names each objective first, so it reads one way.
KR1.1 help replaced by a developer help, the word O1 uses.
No coined term left to define; the O and KR labels are defined by the heading Objectives and key results above them.
No abbreviation beyond the O and KR labels, which the heading spells out.
The order stated in full in the ranking line and the sentence after it.
The KR1.2 and KR2.2 notes taken out, as the ranking line sits right below them and needs no link.
Each kept name written the same way throughout, in code format for invoicer, accountant, installer, and the O and KR labels.

docs/product-vision.md made: KR1.1 says without a developer help; the ranked after notes are gone; the ranking line names KR1.1 first within O1 and KR2.1 first within O2, followed by why O1 and O2 key results have no order between them.

Tried in a throwaway copy as a maintainer looking for the order: grep exit 0; the order appears only in the ranking line and the no-order line after it, with no ranked after note and no bare without help left.
Made written: where each of the twelve decisions and both kept mores land, and two points settled without asking, with their grounds.
